items.q: PTSD can be diagnosed when symptoms persist beyond what duration after trauma?
items.exp: Beyond one month separates PTSD from acute stress disorder (3 days to 1 month). Six months is schizophrenia timeframe distractor.
r: Incorrect. Three days starts acute stress window.
Correct. Over one month is PTSD.
Incorrect. One week remains acute stress.
Incorrect. Six months not required.
items.kp: One month line divides acute stress from PTSD.

items.q: First line treatment for PTSD in adults is what?
items.exp: Trauma focused CBT and EMDR carry strongest guideline support. Drugs are adjunct or second line; benzodiazepines may worsen course and forced debriefing is discouraged.
r: Incorrect. Benzodiazepines worsen PTSD outcomes.
Correct. Trauma focused therapy first.
Incorrect. Antipsychotics only for specific comorbidity.
Incorrect. Debriefing is ineffective or harmful.
items.kp: Process trauma in therapy; do not sedate or force recount.

items.q: Soldier with flashbacks, nightmares, avoiding fireworks, emotional numbness and exaggerated startle 8 months after combat shows which PTSD clusters?
o: All four: intrusion, avoidance, negative mood cognition, hyperarousal
items.exp: The vignette spans intrusion (flashbacks, nightmares), avoidance, negative alterations (numbness) and arousal (startle), fulfilling PTSD pattern beyond one month.
r: Incorrect. Symptoms exceed intrusion alone.
Correct. All four clusters present.
Incorrect. No elevated mood or pressure.
Incorrect. Arousal and intrusion are not negative symptoms.

items.q: Distress 2 months after divorce, tearful and anxious, not meeting depression criteria, resolving as stressor settles, best fits what?
o: Adjustment disorder with mixed anxiety and depressed mood
items.exp: Adjustment disorder follows identifiable stressor within three months, is out of proportion or impairing yet subthreshold for major disorders, and remits within six months of stressor termination.
r: Incorrect. Full criteria explicitly not met.
Correct. Adjustment disorder pattern.
Incorrect. No qualifying trauma or intrusion clusters.
Incorrect. Needs two years chronic low mood.
items.kp: Stressor bound and subthreshold equals adjustment.

items.q: Single session psychological debriefing forced after trauma is recommended how?
items.exp: Trials show compulsory single session debriefing does not prevent PTSD and can increase symptoms by forced re exposure without therapeutic structure; watchful waiting and targeted therapy for persistent symptoms replace it.
r: Incorrect. Mandating is against evidence.
Correct. Avoid forced debriefing.
Incorrect. Children also not forced.
Incorrect. It never substitutes therapy.
items.kp: Do not make everyone relive it once.

items.q: Complex PTSD adds which features beyond core PTSD?
o: Affect dysregulation, negative self concept and relational disturbance
items.exp: ICD complex PTSD includes disturbances in self organisation after prolonged trauma: emotional dysregulation, shame based negative self view and inability to feel close to others, guiding phase based treatment.
r: Incorrect. Psychosis is not defining addition.
Correct. Self organisation disturbance defines complex form.
Incorrect. Mood elevation unrelated.
Incorrect. Amnesia is dissociative feature, not required.
items.kp: Core PTSD plus broken self and relationships equals complex.

items.q: Which drug strategy is guideline supported when PTSD pharmacotherapy is needed?
o: SSRI (or venlafaxine) as adjunct or second line
items.exp: Sertraline and paroxetine class SSRIs and venlafaxine show modest PTSD efficacy as adjuncts when therapy unavailable, declined or insufficient. Prazosin nightmare data are inconsistent after large trials.
r: Incorrect. Large trial failed to confirm prazosin benefit.
Correct. SSRI or venlafaxine second line.
Incorrect. Benzodiazepines harm course.
Incorrect. Antipsychotics lack monotherapy support.
items.kp: Drugs support therapy in PTSD, never sedatives.

items.q: Child after abuse re enacts events repetitively in play, wets bed again and complains of stomach aches. This presentation suggests what?
o: Age appropriate expression of post traumatic stress
items.exp: Children express PTSD through traumatic play re enactment, developmental regression and somatic symptoms rather than verbal flashback reports, needing trauma focused CBT adapted for children and caregiver work.
r: Incorrect. Pattern follows trauma with regression.
Correct. Childhood PTSD expression.
Incorrect. No psychotic phenomena described.
Incorrect. Regression here is trauma linked, not neurodevelopmental course.
items.kp: Children play out trauma they cannot narrate.

items.q: Before trauma processing therapy begins, the essential first phase is what?
o: Safety, stabilisation and coping skills, especially in complex trauma
items.exp: Phase based care establishes current safety (ongoing abuse excluded), stabilisation and regulation skills before memory processing, preventing overwhelm and dropout, then reintegration follows.
r: Incorrect. Recounting without safety destabilises.
Correct. Safety and stabilisation first.
Incorrect. Medicines continue as indicated.
Incorrect. Hypnosis is not required phase.

items.q: Bereavement with yearning, waves of grief tied to reminders, preserved capacity for positive memories, most likely represents what?
o: Normal grief, not adjustment or depressive disorder by itself
items.exp: Normal grief comes in reminder linked waves with preserved self esteem and positive recall, differing from persistent anhedonia and worthlessness of depression. Prolonged grief disorder needs prolonged intense impairment beyond cultural norms (months thresholds vary).
r: Incorrect. Grief waves alone are not depression.
Correct. Normal grief pattern.
Incorrect. No trauma intrusion cluster required.
Incorrect. Most grief is not prolonged disorder.
items.kp: Grief waves with warmth preserved are human, not illness.
